description: Single-panel XRD figure (Fig. 1) presenting four vertically offset diffraction patterns of low-density steels (LDSs) in one set of axes. The x-axis is 2θ (deg) running 30 to 90 with gridline ticks every 10°; the y-axis is Intensity (a.u.) with no numeric ticks, so only relative peak heights within a pattern are comparable. A legend in the top-right corner shows an orange diamond marker labelled "-FCC". The four stacked traces, from top to bottom, are labelled S0 (red), S950 (green), S1050 (blue) and S1150 (magenta), each shifted vertically for clarity. Four sharp reflections are labelled and marked with orange diamonds: (111) just above the 40° gridline, (200) near the 50° gridline, (220) between 70° and 80°, and (311) just below 90°. No additional or secondary-phase peaks are visible in any pattern. The relative intensities change systematically: S0 is dominated by the (220) peak, whereas in S950, S1050 and S1150 the (111) peak becomes the most intense and (220) is markedly weakened. The figure therefore demonstrates that solution treatment preserves a single-phase face-centred-cubic austenitic matrix while altering the relative intensities of the (111) and (220) reflections.
measured_quantities: peak position of FCC (111), (200), (220) and (311) reflections

observations.observation: The figure contains four XRD patterns stacked vertically in one axes, labelled from top to bottom S0 (red), S950 (green), S1050 (blue) and S1150 (magenta).
The x-axis is labelled 2θ (deg) and spans 30 to 90 with gridline ticks at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90; the y-axis is labelled Intensity (a.u.) and carries no numeric ticks or values.
Four reflections are labelled in the plot as (111), (200), (220) and (311), positioned respectively just above the 40° gridline, near the 50° gridline, between 70° and 80°, and just below 90°.
An orange diamond marker on each labelled peak corresponds to the legend entry '-FCC', indicating all four reflections are assigned to a face-centred cubic phase.
No reflection other than the four FCC peaks is visible in any of the four patterns, i.e. no secondary-phase peaks appear.
In the S0 pattern the (220) peak is the most intense reflection, whereas in the S950, S1050 and S1150 patterns the (111) peak is the most intense and the (220) peak is much weaker.
The four patterns are vertically offset within the same axes, so peak heights are comparable only within a single pattern and not quantitatively between samples.
The caption states that the figure shows XRD spectra of the LDSs after solution treatment.
The citing text states that the diffraction peaks reveal a single-phase face-centred cubic (FCC) austenitic structure, confirmed by the presence of (111), (200), (220) and (311) peaks.
The citing text states that solution treatment preserves the austenitic matrix while modifying the relative peak intensities.
The citing text states that the (111) peak intensity significantly increases following solution treatment whereas the (220) peak intensity correspondingly decreases.
